newsitem.title: CHINA: Beijing city economic growth seen 9.1 pct in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Beijing city economic growth seen 9.1 pct in 1996.

text.p: The economy of China's capital, Beijing, is forecast to grow by 9.1 percent in 1996 compared with last year, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.

The city's gross domestic product is expected to reach 160.7 billion yuan this year, up 9.1 percent year-on-year, while gross investment in fixed assets will reach 98.5 billion yuan, up 17.1 percent, it said.

The city has curbed retail price inflation to 7.3 percent, a drop of 5.3 percentage points from last year and the first time the city has driven the retail price index below the economic growth rate since 1993, it said.
The retail sales volume of consumer goods was expected to reach 97.5 billion yuan this year, up 18 percent, it said.
Living standards have improved, with per capita income reaching 6,885 yuan, up by an inflation-adjusted 5.1 percent.
Total savings of the municipality's estimated 11 million urban and rural residents topped 168.07 billion yuan at the end of November, and was expected to reach 170 billion yuan for the year.
Foreign investment in the city was expected to reach a record $2.2 billion this year, it quoted Yi Xiqun, director of the city's foreign economic and trade commission, as saying.
